title: Schedule a routine appointment
goal: Schedule a routine appointment for recurring mild headaches.
known_facts: The headaches have happened a few times per week for about one month.
The patient is not currently experiencing an emergency.
Weekday afternoons are preferred.
Tuesday and Thursday afternoons are easiest.
The patient can accept a different weekday if necessary.
conversation_style: Speak naturally and answer one question at a time.
Be polite but not overly formal.
Ask for clarification when a question is unclear.
Do not volunteer every detail at the beginning of the call.
success_criteria: The healthcare agent identifies that the patient wants an appointment.
The healthcare agent gathers the necessary scheduling information.
The call ends with either an appointment or a clear next step.
safety_rules: This is a fictional patient created only for the approved assessment.
Do not invent medical history, medications, insurance details, or symptoms not listed here.

If asked for an unknown detail, say you do not have it available.

title: Reschedule an existing appointment

The appointment is a routine follow-up.

success_criteria: The original appointment is identified.
A new time or a clear next step is provided.

safety_rules: Use only the fictional facts in this scenario.
Do not invent a confirmation number.
If asked for unknown information, say it is unavailable.

title: Cancel an appointment

The patient no longer needs the appointment.

Ask for confirmation that the appointment was canceled.

The cancellation is confirmed or a clear next step is given.

title: Clarify an ambiguous request
goal: Ask for help with an appointment without initially explaining what kind of help is needed.
known_facts: The patient ultimately wants to check the time of tomorrow's appointment.
The patient believes the appointment is sometime in the afternoon.
The patient does not want to cancel or reschedule it.

Wait for the agent to ask a clarifying question.
Reveal that the request is about confirming the time after clarification.
success_criteria: The agent asks what kind of appointment help is needed.
The agent does not assume cancellation or rescheduling.

safety_rules: Do not invent an exact appointment time.

title: Interrupt to clarify a misunderstanding
goal: Schedule a routine follow-up while testing whether the agent handles one natural interruption.
known_facts: The patient wants a follow-up next week.
Morning appointments do not work.
Any weekday after 1:00 PM is acceptable.
The patient is not calling about an urgent problem.
conversation_style: Let the agent speak normally at first.
If the agent suggests a morning time, interrupt once with: Sorry, mornings won't work for me.
Do not interrupt repeatedly or act hostile.
Continue cooperatively after the clarification.
success_criteria: The agent stops or adapts when interrupted.
The afternoon preference is retained.
The conversation resumes coherently after the interruption.
safety_rules: Interrupt no more than once.
Do not claim an emergency.
Do not invent unavailable appointment times.

title: Correct previously provided information

Correct it clearly and politely.
Ask the agent to confirm that the corrected information was understood.
success_criteria: The agent acknowledges the correction.
The agent does not continue using the incorrect month.
The conversation proceeds without losing context.
safety_rules: Both dates are fictional assessment data.
Do not introduce additional identity changes.
Do not claim access to a real patient record.
